title: Sensex rises 427 points as Nifty Bank hits record close; rupee gains to 93.51
dek: Falling crude prices and foreign buying lifted banks and property stocks for a third straight day of gains, while IT shares fell.
author: Declaration Desk
body:
The Sensex rose 427.40 points, or 0.52%, to close at 82,532.19 on Tuesday, and the Nifty 50 gained 96.30 points, or 0.38%, to 25,387.40, a third straight day of gains, as falling crude prices and buying by foreign investors lifted banks and property stocks. The Nifty Bank index rose 697.35 points, or 1.13%, to 62,273.25, which reports said was a record closing high.

Public-sector banks led the market, with the Nifty PSU Bank index up 1.95%, while realty stocks rose 1.94% and autos 0.72%, according to market reports. Information technology stocks fell, with the Nifty IT index down 0.90%. Adani Enterprises, Eicher Motors, Max Healthcare, Asian Paints and Axis Bank were the biggest gainers in the Nifty 50, and HCL Technologies, Power Grid, HDFC Life, ONGC and Coal India the biggest losers. Smaller companies lagged: the Nifty Smallcap 100 slipped 0.22%, while the Midcap 100 gained 0.25%.

Brent crude for January delivery was trading at about $92.76 a barrel at 3.35 pm, as shipments through the Strait of Hormuz continued to recover, reports said. The rupee rose 43 paise to a provisional close of 93.51 a dollar, according to reports, helped by cheaper oil and foreign inflows.

The gains came despite a sell-off in AI chip stocks that pushed the Nasdaq into a correction overnight and weighed on IT shares in Asia. Wholesale inflation data released on Monday showed prices rising 12.29% in October, driven by fuel and power.
